Rashi on Kiddushin 2a:1:1.english: A woman is acquired - To her husband.

Rashi on Kiddushin 2a:1:2.hebrew: בשלוש דרכים - כדמפרש ואזיל. והאי שלוש לשון נקבה הוא, ובגמרא בעי: אמאי תנא לשון נקבה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 2a:1:2.english: In three ways - As [the Mishnah] goes on to explain. And this [word] shalosh [three] is in the feminine form, and in the Gemara it asks: Why did [the Tanna] teach in the feminine form?

Rashi on Kiddushin 2a:1:3.hebrew: וקונה את עצמה בשתי דרכים - גרסי':
Rashi on Kiddushin 2a:1:3.english: And she acquires herself in two ways - This is our reading.

Rashi on Kiddushin 2a:1:4.english: And she acquires herself - To be in her own domain to marry another.

Rashi on Kiddushin 2a:1:5.hebrew: בכסף ובשטר - מפרש בברייתא בגמ' (לקמן קידושין דף ה ע"ב): נותן לה כסף או שווה כסף, ואומר לה: הרי את מקודשת לי. שטר — כותב לה על הנייר, אף על פי שאינו שווה פרוטה: הרי את מקודשת לי. ביאה — בא עליה, ואמר: התקדשי לי בביאה זו. וכולהו יליף מקראי:
Rashi on Kiddushin 2a:1:5.english: With money and with a document - It is explained in a baraita in the Gemara (below, Kiddushin 5b): He gives her money or [an item] worth money, and says to her: "You are hereby betrothed to me." [As for a] document — he writes for her on paper, even though it is not worth a peruta: "You are hereby betrothed to me." [As for] intercourse — he engages in intercourse with her, and says: "Be betrothed to me through this act of intercourse." And [the Gemara] derives all of them from verses.

Rashi on Kiddushin 2a:1:6.english: The reasoning of Beit Shammai is explained in the Gemara (11a).

Rashi on Kiddushin 2a:1:8.english: The Italian issar - [It is made] of silver, and its value is eight perutot.

Rashi on Kiddushin 2a:2:1.english: The yevama is acquired - To the yavam.

Rashi on Kiddushin 2a:2:2.english: Through intercourse - [She is acquired] to be like his wife in every respect, such that if he comes to divorce her afterward, she does not require chalitzah from him, but rather [only] a bill of divorce. However, a document and money are not effective regarding her by Torah law, but only by Rabbinic law, for they instituted that ma'amar [levirate betrothal] is effective regarding her, as we say in Yevamot (50a). However, it does not finalize [the acquisition] of her to [the extent that he would] inherit her and become [ritually] impure for her [if he is a priest], nor to exempt her from chalitzah, but rather [it serves only] to disqualify her for his other brothers.

Rashi on Kiddushin 2a:3:1.hebrew: ומאי שנא התם - בפרק שני (לקמן קידושין דף מא ע"א), דתנא "האיש מקדש בו ובשלוחו" — ניתני הכא "האשה מתקדשת":
Rashi on Kiddushin 2a:3:1.english: And what is different there - In the second chapter (below, Kiddushin 41a), where [the Mishnah] teaches: "A man betroths, [whether] by himself or through his agent" — let it teach here: "A woman is betrothed."

Rashi on Kiddushin 2a:3:2.hebrew: משום דקבעי למיתני כסף - בהני קניינין, ואמרינן לקמן (קידושין דף ד ע"ב): כסף מנלן דנקנית בו? ומפרשינן דגמרינן קיחה קיחה משדה עפרון, דאקרי קניין. הלכך, תנא הכא קניין:
Rashi on Kiddushin 2a:3:2.english: Because he wanted to teach [about] money - Among these [modes of] acquisition; and we say later on (Kiddushin 4b): "From where do we [derive that] she is acquired with money?" And we explain that we derive [it from] "taking" [and] "taking" from the field of Ephron, which is called an "acquisition." Therefore, [the tanna] taught "acquisition" here.

Rashi on Kiddushin 2a:4:1.hebrew: וכסף מנלן - לאו הכא קא בעי לה, אלא לקמן (קידושין דף ג ע"ב). והכא, האי מתרץ קאמר לה לכולא מילתא: משום דקא בעי למיתני כסף, וכסף מנלן — ילפינן ליה לקמן (קידושין דף ד ע"ב) מקיחה, וקיחה לשון קניין הוא. הילכך, תני האשה נקנית:
Rashi on Kiddushin 2a:4:1.english: And from where do we [derive] money - It is not here that [the Gemara] asks this, but rather later on (Kiddushin 3b). And here, this answerer states the entire matter: Because he wanted to teach [about] money; and [as for] money, from where do we [derive it]? We derive it later on (Kiddushin 4b) from "taking," and "taking" is an expression of acquisition. Therefore, [the Tanna] taught: "A woman is acquired."

Tosafot on Kiddushin 2a:1:1.english: A woman is acquired - Here [the Tanna] teaches with a hei [the definite article]. And so in several places, regarding a man and a woman, it teaches with a hei. Such as: "The woman who went" (Yevamot 114b), "The woman whose husband went" (ibid. 67b), "The woman who was widowed" (Ketubot 15b), "The man betroths" (below, Kiddushin 41a). And this is difficult: For in that which we learned [in the Mishnah], "A virgin is married" (Ketubot 2a) — why does it not teach, "The virgin is married"? And one can say that here it refers to the verse, meaning: the woman who is specified in the verse, for we find a woman specified in the verse regarding marriage, as it is written: "When a man takes a woman" [Deuteronomy 24:1]; but "a virgin" does not refer to a verse, for we do not find anywhere in Scripture "a virgin" explicitly regarding marriage. However, this is difficult: Below (Kiddushin 14b) where we learned [in the Mishnah], "A Hebrew slave," "A Canaanite slave" (22b), "A Hebrew maidservant" (14b) — why does it not teach them with a hei? For they are indeed specified in the verse! And perhaps regarding these, a slave and a maidservant, the usage of a hei does not apply to them, as they are not so clearly specified, since [the Tanna] had to specify regarding them which of them [is meant]: whether a Hebrew [slave] or a Canaanite [slave], or whether a Hebrew [maidservant] or a Canaanite [maidservant]; for regarding a yevamah, it teaches "The yevamah." And one should not be so concerned [about this], for in every place the Tanna teaches the phrasing that flows fluently in his mouth. For so we find that there are places where he teaches the subject before the number — like this case here, and so too: "A virgin is married on the fourth day," "An etrog is similar to a tree in three ways," and "The Torah is acquired through forty-eight things" (Avot 6:5); and there are places where he teaches the number first — such as: "With ten utterances [the world was created]" (ibid. 5:1), "On the light of the fourteenth, one searches [for chametz]" (Pesachim 2a), "Seven days prior to Yom Kippur" (Yoma 2a), "In seven ways they examine a zav" (Zavim 2:2), and "In three matters bills of divorce for women are equal to bills of emancipation for slaves" (Gittin 9a).

Tosafot on Kiddushin 2a:1:2.hebrew: ב"ש אומרים בדינר - במס' עדויות (פ"ד מ"ז) תני ליה גבי קולי ב"ש וחומרי ב"ה. ואע"ג דאי קבלה קדושין מאחר הוו ב"ש לחומרא — מיהו לאו להכי מיתשיל, כדאמרינן ביומא (פ:): כי אתשיל לעניין עוג מלך הבשן:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 2a:1:2.english: Beit Shammai say: With a dinar - In Tractate Eduyot (4:7), this is taught among the leniencies of Beit Shammai and the stringencies of Beit Hillel. And although, if she accepted betrothal from another [man], Beit Shammai would be stringent — nevertheless, it was not asked regarding this [case], as we say in Yoma (80b): "When it was asked, [it was asked] with regard to Og, king of Bashan."

Tosafot on Kiddushin 2a:1:3.hebrew: בפרוטה ובשווה פרוטה - תימה: דלא הוה למיתני אלא בשווה פרוטה, כדתנן בהזהב (ב"מ ד' נה.): "חמשה פרוטות הן: ההודאה בשווה פרוטה, והאשה מתקדשת בשווה פרוטה"! וי"ל: משום דתנא כאן בכסף — מפרש באיזה כסף: דינר לב"ש, ופרוטה לב"ה. ולפי שלא נטעה לומר כסף דווקא, ולא שווה כסף — כדיליף "קיחה" "קיחה" משדה עפרון דכתיב ביה כסף — מפרש שווה כסף. וא"ת: ומנא לן דשווה כסף ככסף? דהא לקמן (קידושין טז.) מיבעי ליה קרא גבי עבד עברי: "ישיב" — לרבות שוה כסף ככסף; ופדיון הבן דכתיב ביה כסף, ואמר לקמן (קידושין ח.) דרב כהנא שקל סודרא בפדיון הבן — ומנא לן דשווה כסף ככסף? ומיהו בפרק קמא דשבועות (דף ד ע"ב) דריש כלל ופרט וכלל. אבל גבי ערכין דכתיב ביה כסף, והקדש נמי — דתנן (ערכין דף כז.) גבי המקדיש שדה, שהקדש נפדה בכסף ובשווה כסף — מנלן דשווה כסף ככסף? מיהו בהקדשות נמי אפשר דדרשינן כלל ופרט וכלל, דהא אין הקדש נפדה בקרקע, כדאמרינן בהזהב (ב"מ נד.): "הרי אמרו אין הקדש מתחלל ע"ג קרקע, דרחמנא אמר: ונתן הכסף וקם לו", ולקמן (קידושין ה.) נמי אמרינן דאין פודין הקדש ומעשר שני בשטר — אבל גבי קדושין וערכין מנלן דשווה כסף ככסף? וי"ל: דילפינן מע"ע. וא"ת: והא גבי נזיקין נמי כתב קרא "כסף ישיב לבעליו", ודרשינן בפ"ק דב"ק (דף ז ע"א): "ישיב" — לרבות שווה כסף ככסף, וא"כ הוו נזיקין ועבד עברי שני כתובין הבאין כאחד, ואין מלמדין! ויש לומר: דתרוייהו צריכי: דאי כתב עבד עברי גרידא, לא מצי למילף נזיקין מיניה, לפי שמצינו שהקפיד הכתוב לעניין מיטב, וסד"א נמי כסף דווקא ולא שויו — להכי איצטריך "כסף ישיב" גבי נזיקין; וגבי ע"ע איצטריך נמי קרא, דלא מצי יליף מנזיקין, דהוה אמינא: עבד דומיא דנזיקין, ואם מיקני בקרקע ליבעי מיטב — לכך איצטריך תרוייהו. אי נמי י"ל: אי כתב בעבד, הוה אמינא דדין הוא שנקל עליו דיכול לפדות עצמו אפי' בשווה כסף, כדי שלא יטמע בין העובדי כוכבים; אבל גבי נזיקין, דלא שייך למימר כך, לא אמרינן הכי. ואי כתב בנזיקין גרידא, לא מצי למילף עבד מיניה — דס"ד דלא יהיה שווה כסף ככסף בעבד, לפי שגם הוא גרם לו לימכר על שנשא ונתן בפירות שביעית, וכר' יוסי בר' חנינא דלקמן (קידושין דף כ ע"א), וס"ד דנחמיר עליו לומר: דווקא כסף ולא שוויו. והא דאיצטריך קרא לפדיון הבן והקדש, דשווה כסף ככסף, ולא יליף מנזיקין וע"ע — לפי שבא למעט קרקעות ושטרות, שאין פודין בהן בכור אדם והקדשות:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 2a:1:3.english: "With a perutah and with the value of a perutah" - It is puzzling: for it should have taught only "with the value of a perutah," as we learned in [the chapter] HaZahav (Bava Metzia 55a): "Five [rulings concerning] perutot are [stated in the Mishnah]: an admission [to a claim must be] with the value of a perutah, and a woman is betrothed with the value of a perutah"! And one can say: Because it taught here [at the beginning of the Mishnah] "with money" — it explains with what [amount of] money: a dinar according to Beit Shammai, and a perutah according to Beit Hillel. And so that we should not err in saying [that betrothal requires] actual money specifically and not the value of money — as [the Gemara] derives [via a verbal analogy of] "taking" [and] "taking" from the field of Ephron, regarding which "money" is written — it explains [that it may also be with] the value of money. And if you should say: But from where do we know that the value of money is like money [for betrothal]? For later (Kiddushin 16a), a verse is required regarding a Hebrew slave: "[he shall] return" — to include the value of money as money; and [regarding] the redemption of the [firstborn] son, concerning which "money" is written, and [yet] it says later (Kiddushin 8a) that Rav Kahana accepted a scarf for the redemption of the son — from where do we know that the value of money is like money? However, in the first chapter of Shevuot (4b), it expounds [the verses of redemption of the son through the hermeneutical rule of] a general proposition, a detail, and a general proposition. But regarding valuations, in which "money" is written, and consecrated property as well — as we learned (Arakhin 27a) regarding one who consecrates a field, that consecrated property is redeemed with money and with the value of money — from where do we know that the value of money is like money? However, regarding consecrated property it is also possible that we expound a general proposition, a detail, and a general proposition, for consecrated property cannot be redeemed with land, as we say in HaZahav (Bava Metzia 54a): "Behold, they said: consecrated property is not deconsecrated onto land, for the Merciful One said: 'Then he shall give the money, and it shall be assured to him'", and later (Kiddushin 5a) we also say that one does not redeem consecrated property or second tithe with a promissory note — but regarding betrothal and valuations, from where do we know that the value of money is like money? And one can say: We derive [them] from a Hebrew slave. And if you should say: But regarding damages as well, the verse wrote: "He shall restore money to its owner," and we expound in the first chapter of Bava Kamma (7a): "'He shall restore' — to include the value of money as money"; and if so, damages and Hebrew slave are two verses that come as one, and [the rule is that] two verses that come as one do not teach [their rule to other cases]! And one can say: Both of them are needed: For had [the Torah] written [this] regarding a Hebrew slave alone, one could not derive damages from it, because we find that Scripture was particular regarding [paying from] the best quality [land], and I might have thought that [damages requires] money specifically and not its value — for this reason "he shall restore money" was needed regarding damages; and regarding a Hebrew slave a verse was also needed, for one could not derive [it] from damages, as I would have thought that a slave is similar to damages, and if he is acquired with land, he should require the best quality [land] — therefore both of them were needed. Alternatively, one can say: Had it written [it only] regarding a slave, I would have thought that it is logical that we should be lenient with him, so that he can redeem himself even with the value of money, in order that he should not assimilate among the gentiles; but regarding damages, where it is not applicable to say this, we would not say so. And had it written [it] regarding damages alone, one could not derive slave from it — for it might enter your mind that the value of money should not be like money regarding a slave, because he himself caused himself to be sold on account of having engaged in commerce with the produce of the Sabbatical year, in accordance with Rabbi Yosei bar Rabbi Chanina later (Kiddushin 20a), and it might enter your mind that we should be strict with him to say: specifically money and not its value. And as for that which a verse was needed for the redemption of the son and consecrated property, [to teach] that the value of money is like money, and it is not derived from damages and Hebrew slave — [that is] because it comes to exclude land and promissory notes, with which one does not redeem a human firstborn or consecrated property.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 2a:1:4.hebrew: וכמה היא פרוטה - הא דלא מפרש כמה הוא דינר, משום דדינר היו יודעין כמה היה — שהוא אחד מכ"ד בדינר של זהב, כדאמרינן בריש הזהב (ב"מ נד:). אבל פרוטה — איכא פלוגתא בגמרא לקמן (קידושין דף יב ע"א): זימנין דזיילי, וזימנין דייקרי. ועוד, דדברי ב"ה, דקי"ל כוותיה, איבעי ליה לפרושי טפי:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 2a:1:4.english: "And how much is a perutah?" - The reason that [the Mishnah] does not explain how much a dinar is, is that regarding a dinar, they knew how much it was — that it is one twenty-fourth of a gold dinar, as we say at the beginning of [the chapter] HaZahav (Bava Metzia 54b). However, [regarding] a perutah, there is a dispute in the Gemara later (Kiddushin 12a), [since] at times [the issars] depreciated and at times they appreciated. And furthermore, [as for] the words of Beit Hillel, since we rule in accordance with them, [the Tanna] needed to explain [their position] more.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 2a:1:5.english: "One-eighth of an issar" - [This is] when the issars are at their standard [value], but when the issars depreciate: [it is] one-sixth, as we say in the Gemara (ibid.).

Tosafot on Kiddushin 2a:1:6.hebrew: איטלקי - מפרש ר"ת: על שם איטליא של יון, ואין לתמוה על הקו"ף, כדאשכחנא (עזרא ד,ט): "שושנכיא" — על שם שושן:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 2a:1:6.english: "Italian" - Rabbeinu Tam explains: [It is named] after "Italia of Greece," and one should not wonder about the [letter] kuf [in italki], as we find (Ezra 4:9): "Shushankhaye" — [named] after Shushan.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 2a:2:1.hebrew: היבמה נקנית כו' - תימה דלא תני מניינא כדלעיל, וליתני: "נקנית בדרך אחד וקונה עצמה בשני דרכים". וכמו מניינא דלעיל למעוטי, כדאמרינן בגמרא — האי מניינא נמי למעוטי: דרישא — למעוטי כסף ושטר, כדדריש לקמן (קידושין יד.): "ביאה גומר ואין כסף ושטר גומרין בה"; ומניינא דסיפא — למעוטי ג"כ, דלא נילף מק"ו מאשה, כדאמרינן בגמ' (שם) דדרשינן: "נעלו — אין, מידי אחרינא — לא". וי"ל, דבחדא מילתא אין לשנות מניינא. ואע"ג דגבי אתרוג תנן "ששוה לאילן בג' דרכים ולירק בדרך אחד" — התם בא לפרש דברים החולקים בו. ומאחר דלא תנא מניינא ביבמה, לא חש לשנות מניינא בעבד עברי וכנעני; אי נמי, משום דלא איצטריך למיתני בהם מניינא למעוטי מידי:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 2a:2:1.english: "A yevama is acquired, etc." - It is puzzling that [the Mishnah] does not teach a count as above, and let it teach: "She is acquired in one way and acquires herself in two ways." And just as the count above comes to exclude [other methods], as we say in the Gemara, this count would also come to exclude: that of the first clause [would come] to exclude money and a document, as [the Gemara] expounds below (Kiddushin 14a): "Intercourse completes [her acquisition], and money and a document do not complete [her acquisition]"; and the count of the latter clause [would come] to exclude as well, so that we should not derive [that she can leave through a bill of divorce] from an a fortiori inference [kal vaḥomer] from an [ordinary married] woman, as we say in the Gemara (ibid.) that we expound: "[With] his shoe — yes; [with] anything else — no." And one can say that for a single matter [i.e., when there is only one method], [the Mishnah] does not state a count. And even though with regard to an etrog we learn: "Which is similar to a tree in three ways and to a vegetable in one way" — there, it comes to specify the matters that divide its status [between a tree and a vegetable]. And since [the Mishnah] did not teach a count with regard to a yevama, it was not concerned to state a count with regard to a Hebrew slave and a Canaanite [slave]; alternatively, because it was not necessary to teach a count with regard to them to exclude anything.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 2a:3:1.hebrew: מאי שנא הכא דתנן האישה נקנית - המ"ל: אגב דבעי למיתני סיפא "וקונה את עצמה", דלא שייך התם לשון קדושין — וכה"ג משני בסמוך. ומיהו אומר הר"ר מנוח, דה"מ למיתני "וניתרת בשני דרכים", דגבי קדושין שייך לשון היתר:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 2a:3:1.english: What is different here that [the Mishnah] teaches: "A woman is acquired" - [The Gemara] could have said: Since [the tanna] needed to teach in the latter clause, "And she acquires herself," where the terminology of betrothal does not apply — and [the Gemara] answers similarly nearby. However, Rabbi Manoach says that [the tanna] could have taught, "And she is released through two ways," for regarding betrothal, the terminology of release applies.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 2a:3:2.hebrew: משום דקבעי למיתני כסף - והכא לא שייך למיפרך: "ותנא תרתי אטו חדא?", כדפריך לקמן — דלשון קניין שייך נמי בשטר וביאה. ולא היה תמוה על לשון קניין, אלא משום דלקמן תנא לשון קדושין והכא תנא לשון קניין. אי נמי: בשטר נמי אשכחן לשון קניין, דכתיב: "ואקח את ספר המקנה" (ירמיהו ל״ב:י״א):
Tosafot on Kiddushin 2a:3:2.english: "Because he wanted to teach [about] money" - And here it is not applicable to object: "And did [the Tanna] teach two on account of one?", as [the Gemara] objects later — for the terminology of acquisition also applies to a document and intercourse. And [the Gemara] was not puzzled by the terminology of acquisition [itself], but only because later [the Tanna] taught the terminology of betrothal, whereas here he taught the terminology of acquisition. Alternatively: regarding a document as well, we find the terminology of acquisition, as it is written: "And I took the deed of purchase [sefer hamiknah]" (Jeremiah 32:11).

Tosafot on Kiddushin 2a:4:1.hebrew: וכסף מנלן גמר קיחה קיחה משדה עפרון - ואם תאמר: ומה צריך לכל זה, לא היה צריך לומר אלא: "כסף איקרי קניין, דכתיב: נתתי כסף השדה קח ממני, וכתיב: השדה אשר קנה אברהם, אי נמי: שדות בכסף יקנו"? וי"ל: דבהכי לא סגי; דנהי דכסף השדה איקרי קניין — כסף דאשה לא איקרי קניין. לכך צריך להביא ראיה דאותו כסף דגמרינן אשה מיניה אקרי קניין:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 2a:4:1.english: "And from where do we [derive that] money [effects betrothal]? It is derived [by a verbal analogy of] 'taking' 'taking' from the field of Ephron" - And if you say: Why is all of this needed, when it only needed to say: "Money is called an acquisition [kinyan], as it is written: 'I will give money for the field; take it from me,' and it is written: 'The field which Abraham acquired'; or alternatively: 'Fields shall be bought with money'"? And one can say: This would not suffice; for granted that the money of a field is called an acquisition [kinyan] — the money of a woman [i.e., for betrothal] is not called an acquisition. Therefore, it is necessary to bring proof that that very money from which we derive [the betrothal of] a woman is called an acquisition.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 2a:4:2.hebrew: וכתיב התם נתתי כסף השדה קח ממני - אינו חושש אלא שמוצא לשון קיחה, אע"ג דלא דמי — דקיחה דהכא קיימא אכסף של שדה, וקיחה דאשה לא קיימא אכסף של אשה אלא אאשה עצמה. וא"ת: וליתני "האשה נקחת", שהוא לישנא דקרא טפי, דכתיב "כי יקח"; ותנן נמי עירובין (כו:): "הכל נקח בכסף מעשר"; וביאה — שייך נמי לשון קיחה, דכתיב (ויקרא כ,יז): "ואיש אשר יקח את אחותו"? וי"ל, דלא שייך למיתני סיפא: "ולוקחת עצמה בב' דרכים":
Tosafot on Kiddushin 2a:4:2.english: "And it is written there: 'I give the money for the field; take it from me'" - [The Gemara] is unconcerned [about the difference], requiring only that it find the expression of "taking," even though they are not comparable: for the "taking" here applies to the money of the field, whereas the "taking" of a woman does not apply to the money for the woman, but rather to the woman herself. And if you should say: Then let [the Mishnah] teach, "A woman is taken," which is closer to the language of Scripture, as it is written: "When a man takes [a woman]" (Deuteronomy 24:1); and we also learned in Eruvin (26b): "Everything is taken [i.e., purchased] with [second-]tithe money"; and regarding intercourse, the term "taking" also applies, as it is written (Leviticus 20:17): "And if a man takes his sister"? And one can answer: That it would not be appropriate to teach in the concluding clause: "and she takes herself in two ways."
